Title: August 6, 2026 City of Boulder City Council Meeting

Topic1.Title: Open Comment
Topic1.Summary: Eleven residents signed up to speak during open comment on topics including Palestine and genocide, the Fort Chambers site interpretive design and the Sand Creek massacre, the Spruce Pool and South Boulder Rec Center, permanently affordable housing HOA costs, and shelter bathroom sanitary conditions. Staff responded that they will follow up on the Fort Chambers site, Spruce Pool closure timing, HOA affordability, and shelter conditions. Council members raised questions about tribal consultations and investment portfolio issues. Open comment closed before the business portion of the meeting resumed.

Topic2.Title: Consent Agenda and Call-Up Check-Ins
Topic2.Summary: Council approved the consent agenda, items 3A through 3C, by unanimous vote. No items were called up during the call-up check-ins for outside city utility permit requests at 1098 Cherryville Road, 6906 Frying Pan Road, and 5083 Cottonwood Drive.

Topic3.Title: Ballot Measure Staff Presentation and Public Hearing
Topic3.Summary: Staff presented five potential November 2026 ballot measures: the recreation and safety bond, a residential vacancy excise tax, a debt limit charter amendment, firefighter collective bargaining charter language, and a downtown development authority (DDA). Public comments on the measures were heard from dozens of residents and business owners, with strong opinions on both sides, especially regarding the DDA and South Boulder Rec Center amenities. Council considered each ordinance in turn.

Topic4.Title: Firefighter Collective Bargaining Charter Amendment (Ordinance 8761)
Topic4.Summary: Council unanimously adopted Ordinance 8761, referring to the November 3, 2026 ballot a charter amendment adding Section 73 guaranteeing full-time fire department employees the right to bargain collectively. The measure was reached through agreement between city staff and the firefighters union, Local 900.

Topic5.Title: Recreation and Safety Bond (Ordinance 8758)
Topic5.Summary: Council approved Ordinance 8758, a $400 million general obligation bond to fund community recreation, public safety, and capital projects. Council amended the language to specify a lap pool in place of general aquatic amenities for the South Boulder Rec Center. Staff explained the bond would fund projects including South Boulder Rec Center replacement, North Boulder Rec Center renovation, and public safety building replacement. The amendment passed and the ordinance was approved unanimously.

Topic6.Title: Residential Vacancy Excise Tax (Ordinance 8759)
Topic6.Summary: Council adopted Ordinance 8759 by a 7-1 vote, referring to the November ballot a proposed excise tax on homes occupied 183 days or less per year, set at $4,000 per unit starting January 1, 2028 and adjusted annually for inflation. Council member Spear voted no, and Council member Nicole Speer's opposition was based on preferring a fee approach. Council member Tina expressed support for exemptions to be developed in later ordinances.

Topic7.Title: Debt Limit Charter Amendment (Ordinance 8762)
Topic7.Summary: Council unanimously approved Ordinance 8762, referring to the ballot a charter amendment changing the city's debt limit calculation from assessed value to actual value. Staff noted this aligns Boulder with other Colorado municipalities and state statute.

Topic8.Title: Downtown Development Authority (Ordinance 8763)
Topic8.Summary: Council considered Ordinance 8763 to form a downtown development authority covering downtown and University Hill, with tax increment financing and a 3.674 mill levy. Staff explained the DDA would be governed by a board appointed by council and would require three ballot questions. Council voted 4-4 on the motion to refer it to the ballot, so it failed. A motion to direct staff to scope next steps for community engagement on the DDA was supported by six members.

Topic9.Title: Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan Update
Topic9.Summary: Council reviewed the remaining conditions of approval and recommended amendments to the Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan update, following reviews by planning board, the county planning commission, and the Board of County Commissioners. Council unanimously approved the planning board conditions, BOCC conditions, and recommended amendments. Council member Nicole requested that the history section be considered later as a council resolution. Staff noted some items will return to other bodies for further review.
